text:
jen-support: ACME reporting intermittent 502s after we rotated their leaf certs for the private VPC. Started ~10:12 UTC. Their stack: customer nginx -> customer haproxy -> redwood private endpoint. Can someone triage? cc @sam-eng

sam-eng: Do we have any curl/openssl output from the customer? Also any rotator logs for the upload?

jen-support: Paste from their dev: ```openssl s_client -connect acme-private.redwood:443 -servername app.acme.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 C = US, O = Acme, CN = app.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/C=US/O=Acme/CN=app.acme.internal
   i:/C=US/O=Acme Intermediate/CN=Acme Intermediate CA
---
```They only see the leaf in the chain (no intermediate sent).

lee-infra: I checked rotator logs - rotator-bot reports upload completed and bundle included intermediates at 10:05. rotator-bot: `upload OK sha256=abc123 fullchain.pem contains 2 certs`

rotator-bot: rotator: bundle abc123 staged -> active at 2026-06-11T10:06:02Z (fullchain present)

sam-eng: If rotator uploaded the fullchain but openssl sees only leaf, likely a mid-proxy (haproxy/nginx) is serving a different certificate file or a truncated .pem. Common in setups where haproxy uses per-SNI certs from a directory - an older cert without intermediate can be selected for resumed sessions. Can the customer show their haproxy config or output of `haproxy -vv` and `ls /etc/haproxy/certs`?

jen-support: Customer confirmed haproxy maintained a certs dir with an old `app.acme.internal.pem` and the operator hadn't reloaded haproxy after we rotated. They rely on keepalives and session resumption for long-lived backends.

lee-infra: That matches a known pattern: haproxy will pick cert at handshake, but TLS session resumption can resume without re-evaluating SNI mapping in some configs, or a stale cert file may remain on disk. Quick remediation is to reload haproxy so it picks the updated fullchain PEM. Also advise removing old PEMs.

jen-support: Customer restarted haproxy a few minutes ago and confirms errors stopped. They want a permanent checklist so this doesn't recur during future rotations.

sam-eng: We should not trigger remote restarts for customer infra. Action items: 1) Update KB for Private customers: include explicit pre-rotation checklist to verify fronting proxies have fullchain + recommend reload window. 2) Add a rotator enhancement (ROT-312): add post-upload verification that the active endpoint serves the full chain (if reachable) and publish a checksum in the rotator event so customers can validate. I'll open ROT-312 and assign to eng-infra.

jen-support: I told the customer to keep the old certs out of the certs dir and to schedule a reload as part of rotation. They're OK with that and we'll close the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
